title: Choose the visual world for Nexyra
question: The roll assigned The Case Register. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All four sketches show the same worklist screen with the same synthetic data.

options.label: The Case Register
options.thesis: Every case is a ruled entry: an owner, a deadline, an evidence line, and a state that is stamped rather than coloured.
options.detail: Blue-black ink for the entry, a red margin rule carrying the ref, state as a stamp in the last column (double-ruled when escalated), sparse verdigris. Archivo Narrow holds a dense table without turning it into a spreadsheet; Spline Sans Mono carries refs, deadlines and citations.
options.viewport: A full-height ledger sheet. Left: the programme index in navy with the demo clock and open/unowned counts. Right: the case register itself, one ruled entry per case, deadline column right of the stage, state stamped at the far edge. The two escalated entries are overstamped in red at the top of the sheet.
options.signature: The stamp column. State is never a coloured pill: it is a stamped word, doubled or offset when a deadline has been missed, so urgency reads at a glance down the right edge of the sheet.
options.risk: Ledger warmth drifts into nostalgia if the stamp is the only idea; the column discipline has to carry the screen on its own.

raised.raise: Every extracted value now prints with a provenance stamp: source quote, character offset, and the reading session.
The register gains a fixed-scale stage strip: one case read across the seven stages on the same columns, so progress compares without opening anything.
Outreach attempts print as a ruled log with running times, each attempt ending clean against its deadline.
A case detail opens as one entry owning the full sheet; the register stays one move away.

options.label: Flight Strip Rack
options.thesis: A case is a strip in a rack: it belongs to a bay, it moves between bays, and it never leaves the board.
options.detail: Dark control-room ground, paper-cream strips at full contrast, amber for due, oxide red for late, a deadline time ruler across the top. Archivo Narrow sets the strip names; Spline Sans Mono sets times and refs. Standard web controls, no bezel.
options.viewport: Four bays across the screen — Unowned, In flight, Waiting on lab, Closure review — with a day ruler above and the demo clock in the header. Strips stack in each bay; the overdue strip is hatched and pinned to the top of In flight.
options.signature: Bay movement. Sorting and ownership changes are drawn as a strip leaving one rack and landing in another, so the daily job of Nexyra is visible in the layout rather than reported in a chart.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on; effective, familiar, and it needs the strip typography to be flawless to earn its place.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.lineage: spectroscopy plates: hairline emission lines on a calibrated continuum
options.thesis: Deadlines drawn as one rail per stage: every case is a line, and its state is height, dash, and doubling.
options.detail: Near-white continuum with a measured rail, lanes for the four stages, x-position as deadline, weight as state. Archivo for labels, Spline Sans Mono for the axis and citations. Reads as a working product with a real time model.
options.viewport: KPI row, filter bar, then four stage lanes over a five-day axis with a 'now' rule at 27.6%. Each case is a line running to its deadline; the selected line sits on a sodium-yellow plate and opens a case sheet at the lower right.
options.signature: State without colour: a doubled line is past deadline, a dashed line is pending, a half-height line is stale (no accession event in 40h). Escalation is a shape, not a badge.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: timers and escalation are the product's mechanism, and the rail makes them spatial. Holds audience identification; loses narrowly to the register on scanability for a long list.
options.risk: A rail is a chart, and charts are read slower than rows by staff working 140 cases; the list view must stay one click away.

options.label: Cell Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The programme as a visible grid: one case per cell, one monumental figure, one accent plane earned by the deadline.
options.detail: White ground with the construction grid left visible, hard 1px cell rules, a single 104px figure, and one blue plane reserved for cases past deadline. Archivo carries display and label alike; Spline Sans Mono annotates.
options.viewport: Programme figure at left, three counts beside it, filters, then a six-across cell grid where each cell is a case with its days-to-deadline as the number. The escalated cell is the only filled plane on the screen.
options.signature: The number in the cell is the deadline, and cells reflow by whole units as cases close: the screen is a countdown you can read as a grid.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and is the most distinctive at thumbnail size; loses on density, since a 142-case register becomes an endless grid and cell text truncates.
options.risk: Only the world's armature survives the Operate limit, so the grid must stay a layout device over standard table controls, not a poster.

options.label: Plate Section
options.lineage: design annuals printed on uncoated stock
options.thesis: Evidence presented as plates: registration marks, hairline credits, one signed stamp.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coordinators do not identify with an exhibition catalogue, and plates need few, large items where the register needs many small ones.
options.kept: The attribution stamp discipline — provenance of every extracted value.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: engraved botanical folios tracking one plant through its seasons
options.thesis: One case followed through every stage at identical scale.
options.case: Reads as an editorial artifact, and cream plus serif is the default this category already wears; the stage idea, however, is the product's own model.
options.kept: Fixed-scale stage strip: the same case compared across stages without scrolling.

options.label: J-Card Tracklist
options.thesis: Attempts ruled like a tracklist, timed to fill the deadline exactly.
options.case: Fuses poorly: handwriting and ballpoint in a clinical record read as unserious, whatever the underlying idea.
options.kept: The outreach ladder as a ruled attempt log with running times against the deadline.

options.label: One Item, Full Frame
options.thesis: One case owns the whole screen; the next is one snap away.
options.case: Fuses badly: an ops screen is a list of 142 cases, not a queue of one; the scroll-snap model hides the programme.
options.kept: Case detail as one entry owning the sheet, with the register one move away.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean operations dashboard: side nav, KPI cards, filterable table, status pills, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar, four KPI cards, a filterable case table with coloured status pills.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other programme dashboard by design.
